metadata.file_name: 171. Depren & Depren (2022). Cross-Cultural Comparisons of the Factors Influencing the High Reading Achievement in Turkey and China: Evidence from PISA 2018.pdf
metadata.title: Cross-Cultural Comparisons of the Factors Influencing the High Reading Achievement in Turkey and China: Evidence from PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata and describes OECD’s two-stage sampling (schools selected with PPS, then students randomly selected within schools). The analytic sample is restricted to Turkey and China (B-S-J-Z) and further reduced by excluding cases with missing values in the selected factors (final counts reported: 4,631 in Turkey and 10,853 in China). The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or replicate weights in the ML steps (Random Forest feature selection and ARF subgroup identification), so it is unclear whether complex survey design was accounted for in estimation. Because the analysis is implemented in R using arf and caret, the paper should clarify whether weights were incorporated; if not, results may reflect unweighted patterns rather than population-representative estimates.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 reading domain data for two countries only: Turkey and China (B-S-J-Z). The dependent variable is derived from PVREAD1 (binary indicator of whether a student’s reading score is at or above the country average). The analytic sample excludes students with missing values in the factor set selected for the ARF analysis, resulting in 4,631 students for Turkey and 10,853 for China (B-S-J-Z).

main_findings.target_variable: Successful reading achievement (PVREAD1 ≥ country average; binary)
top_predictors: Index of economic social cultural status (ESCS)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest feature selection accuracy (10-fold, 5-repeat CV): 75% (Turkey) and 77% (China (B-S-J-Z)); ARF outputs subset success rates: Turkey up to 91% (subset-1) and China up to 95% (subset-1).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (PVREAD1; binary success defined as at/above the country average), the study leveraged meta-cognition (METASPAM), socioeconomic status (ESCS), and learning/ICT-related factors (ICTCLASS, METASUM) to identify student subgroups with substantially higher-than-average reading success, finding that the strongest common drivers across both countries were METASPAM and ESCS while additional country-specific factors (e.g., ICTCLASS in Turkey; PISADIFF and JOYREAD in China) further differentiated high-performing subsets. This indicates that reading improvement strategies should prioritize credibility assessment and summarization skills, while tailoring ICT use and motivation/test-difficulty supports to the national context, though the binary outcome and unreported survey-weight handling limit population-level causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 reading achievement for 15-year-olds in Turkey and China (B-S-J-Z), using PVREAD1 to create a binary “successful” outcome: 1 if a student’s reading score is at or above the country average, otherwise 0. After excluding students with missing values in the selected factor set, the analytic sample comprises 4,631 students (Turkey) and 10,853 (China (B-S-J-Z)). For feature selection, the authors train a Random Forest model with 10-fold, 5-repeat cross-validation and report accuracy of 75% (Turkey) and 77% (China). They then apply the ARF (iterative pruned-tree) method to identify high-success subgroups, reporting success rates up to 91% in Turkey and 95% in China. Key predictors include meta-cognition (assessing credibility) and ESCS, with additional country-specific factors (ICTCLASS and METASUM in Turkey; PISADIFF, JOYREAD, and SMINS in China). Limitations include the use of a binary PV-derived target and the lack of explicit reporting on whether PISA sampling/replicate weights were applied in the ML pipeline.
